issue.title: test_terminates_every_process_shape_and_verifies_death flakes: status 'killed' instead of 'force_killed'
issue.description:
Observed during the sase-1h7 land agent's verification (2026-10-08). sase-1h7.9 note #3 also
listed `terminate_processes` among load/order flakes that passed on re-run.

- Full-lane `just check` (escalated full suite, master 1964a5f01f plus the sase-1h7 landing diff):
  `tests/test_agent_terminate_processes.py::test_terminates_every_process_shape_and_verifies_death`
  failed with `assert result.status == "force_killed"` / `AssertionError: assert 'killed' == 'force_killed'`
  (`result.success is True` and `result.survivors == ()` held).
- Isolated reruns: failed 1 of 2 on the landing tree and passed on the clean tree. The landing
  diff does not touch process termination.

Likely a timing race: a process the test expects to need SIGKILL exits on SIGTERM within the
grace window under some scheduling, so the aggregate status reads `killed`, not
`force_killed`.

issue.creation_reason: Failed in the sase-1h7 landing's full lane and in 1 of 3 isolated runs, then passed on an unchanged tree; no existing bead tracks it.
